description: Five synthetic papers for the index lifecycle integration test; text written for the test, not taken from arXiv.

papers.title: Stepwise Prompting for Arithmetic
sections: 1 Introduction
Chain of thought prompting asks a language model to write intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer.
2 Results
On grade school arithmetic word problems, stepwise prompting raises accuracy for large models while small models gain little.

papers.title: Confidence and Accuracy
sections: 1 Introduction
Calibration asks whether stated confidence matches observed accuracy across many predictions.
2 Method
Expected calibration error bins predictions by confidence and averages the gap between confidence and accuracy per bin.

papers.title: Voting over Reasoning Paths
sections: 1 Introduction
Self consistency samples several reasoning paths at nonzero temperature and selects the most frequent final answer.
2 Analysis
Majority voting over sampled paths is more robust than greedy decoding when individual paths contain errors.

papers.title: Judging with Language Models
sections: 1 Introduction
Using a language model as a judge introduces position bias, verbosity bias, and self preference.
2 Mitigation
Swapping answer order and averaging both judgments reduces position bias in pairwise evaluation.

papers.title: Retrieval for Grounded Answers
sections: 1 Introduction
Retrieval augmented generation conditions answers on documents fetched for each question.
2 Experiments
Reranking retrieved passages with a cross encoder improves the share of answers supported by evidence.
